specGaps: SG-1 (MAJOR — the plugin composition root has no owning task). VERIFIED AT HEAD: plugin/index.ts binds every tool to handlerNotBound (:203, :57-64), never populates its session registry (:71), passes seven hardcoded literals to gateBeforeToolCall (:232-238, incl. verifyInFlightTree: null, which makes the §3.5 freeze UNREACHABLE through the real hook), and registers only 2 of the §5.1:1717 hooks. handleChatMessage (5.4) and initPlugin (8.2) are called by nothing but their own tests, and no manifest task between 9.6 and 13.1 wires them: 9.6 EXPORTS the slug->path tree translation but its own spec places it 'at the wiring layer' without claiming the factory, and 10.1 adds continuation + ask-gate bodies. The plan's 13.1 bullet nevertheless says 'drives the REAL plugin hooks + REAL handlers'. RESOLUTION: the composition root IS 13.1's Step-2 'glue', which is exactly what 'red -> glue fixes -> green (this is the harness proving itself)' names. 13.1 delivers it as ONE exported, opencode-free composition function (proposed conductor/adapter/wiring.ts: `buildConductorHooks(deps)` returning the hook object, with plugin/index.ts reduced to the factory that supplies real deps and calls it — so the wiring is unit-testable with a synthetic PluginInput exactly as gate-wiring.test.ts already does at :331). It binds (a) each tool's `execute` to its committed handleX, (b) the per-call gate snapshot derived LIVE from the session registry + store + config + the live verify marker via 9.6's slug->path translation, (c) chat.message -> handleChatMessage, (d) event -> 10.1's continuation + ask-gate, (e) chat.params/chat.headers/system transform -> inject.ts. STOP-AND-PARK: whether this lands as its own manifest task BEFORE 13.1 is an orchestrator/manifest decision; this spec does not take it. What is NOT open is the alternative of asserting the e2e against handlerNotBound or against handlers called directly around the plugin — the first is impossible, the second makes 'REAL plugin hooks' a lie and the acceptance row (plan 3132) vacuous.

SG-2 (the §3.1 phase-order gate is not at the hook). §3.1:1046 says 'the phase-order gate denies every conductor tool not in `legal`', but gateBeforeToolCall (tools.ts:265, input shape :175-192) has no run/items and never calls legalTools; the enforcement that exists is the per-item handler guard at tools.ts:2332 which throws a legalTools-derived reason. RESOLUTION: 13.1 asserts the OBSERVABLE — an out-of-order conductor tool called through the plugin's tool map THROWS, the message is legalTools-derived (names what IS legal and what is recommended), and NO state file changes — and additionally asserts that hook and handler cannot disagree, by requiring the deny to come from a legalTools verdict computed over the SAME persisted run/items either way. Whether the composition root also lifts the check into tool.execute.before is implementation freedom; two independent legality tables would not be. Raised at the Phase 13 gate.

SG-3 (13.1 cannot be reddened before its dependencies land). Six manifest tasks it drives are NOT_STARTED at HEAD (9.5a, 9.5b, 9.5c, 9.6, 10.1, and 12.1). RESOLUTION: 13.1 is authored and executed LAST among them, in the manifest order the HANDOFF already records ('Then 10.1, 12, 13, 14, 15'). This spec is promoted now so those tasks are built against a written end-state, but the red for e2e.test.ts is not constructible earlier and MUST NOT be parked in staging in the meantime (a parked red over six moving surfaces would rot).

SG-4 (scenario 5's 'report refuses' is unconstructible as literally written). The plan says 'an item blocks (test repair exhausted), report refuses'. At HEAD, core/gates-phase.ts:172 isSettled counts `blocked !== null` as SETTLED and :355-357 legalizes conductor_report when every item is settled, so a run whose ONLY unfinished item is blocked closes `done` — it never refuses and never reaches the futile-re-prompt path. cannotEverPublish (:192-208) deliberately does NOT treat a blocked dependency as stuck, precisely so the run waits for conductor_answer. RESOLUTION (no plan edit, no code change): scenario 5's queue carries TWO items — A (behavioral, testScope its own test file) and B with `dependsOn: ["A"]`. A blocks at RED on test-repair exhaustion; B is then neither settled nor stuck, so allSettled is false, report REFUSES, B has no stage tool, `recommended` is null, and the continuation engine's re-prompts are genuinely futile. This is the ONLY queue shape in which every clause of the plan's scenario-5 sentence is simultaneously true against committed code, and it is also the shape that makes the scenario worth having (a run stalled behind a blocked dependency is the real wedge). Recorded as a plan-silence resolution and raised at the Phase 13 gate.

SG-5 (scenario 1's report content vs its 2-item queue). §13.1 asks the report to be asserted on 'taints/deferred/exclusions/questions, metrics present', but the same bullet fixes the queue at 'decompose(2 items, disjoint scopes)' and both items PUBLISH, so nothing is deferred and — in a virgin fixture — nothing is excluded either, which would leave three of the four sections trivially empty and the assertion undiscriminating. RESOLUTION, without inventing a third item the plan does not authorize: (i) TAINTS are made non-empty by the override the same bullet requires ('an override exercised once and visible in the report'); (ii) EXCLUSIONS are made non-empty by seeding the fixture's workspace stale-red registry with ONE pre-existing entry before the run starts — realistic (§2.11's registry survives runs), and it exercises the run-start disclosure (run.excludedStaleRed) as well as the report's; (iii) QUESTIONS are made non-empty by one conductor_surface call with `blocksItems: []` (legal — handleSurface's loop at tools.ts:800-810 is a no-op on an empty list, and an open question does not gate the report, only unsettled ITEMS do); (iv) DEFERRED is asserted as present-and-explicitly-none, with the non-empty deferred rendering left to 9.5b's unit row 9.5b-report-md-per-item, which already pins 'every deferred item with its reason'. Recorded so a later reader does not mistake the empty deferred section for missing coverage.

SG-6 (13.1 does not exercise 12.2's setup flow). The §13.1 bullet never mentions conductor_setup, and legalTools with repoConfigured=false (gates-phase.ts:246-250) would make setup the only legal tool — i.e. driving the whole pipeline requires a configured repo anyway. RESOLUTION: the fixture WRITES .conductor/config.json directly (the §2.1 shape, with verify.scopes.unit + itemTest, behavioralPaths ['src/**'], requiredScopes [{pattern:'**',scopes:['unit']}], git {mode:'commit', branchPolicy:'pin', preexistingDirty:'exclude'}, workflow knobs sized small, parallel.writes per scenario, models.default a fixture string) and repoConfigured is true throughout. The setup flow is 12.2's own red. Recorded so the omission is a decision, not a hole.

SG-7 (G14 and the bun leg). scripts/test-conductor.sh:71-86 runs bun over ONE file, conductor/tests/bun-smoke.test.ts; the rest of the suite is Node-only in the gate. RESOLUTION: 13.1 discharges G14 BY CONSTRUCTION — the e2e and the composition root use no Bun shell (`$`), no bun-only API, and reach git and the test runner only through the committed execFileSync-argv discipline (gitio.ts:36/:58-85), which is the property §3.3:1301 actually demands. ADDING e2e.test.ts to the bun leg is an orchestrator decision and is NOT taken here (a five-scenario e2e spawning real child processes is the wrong shape for a runtime smoke, and a second full run would roughly double the gate's wall clock). STOP-AND-PARK if the orchestrator wants it.

SG-8 (canned outputs must not become a private schema). A no-model e2e can silently degrade into a fake pipeline if the canned SDK replies bypass the validation the handlers apply to real model output. RESOLUTION: every canned reply is a STRING the fake SDK returns exactly as a model would (the fake-sdk PromptReply shape), and it is validated by the handlers' own SCHEMAS on the way in — the e2e asserts at least one canned reply is rejected-and-retried by the real validator (a deliberately malformed CLASSIFICATION on the first attempt) so the validation seam is proven live rather than assumed. Additionally the fake's responder is keyed by role + requested schema and returns NO reply for an unexpected dispatch, so a handler that fans out somewhere the script did not anticipate fails the test loudly instead of hanging or silently receiving someone else's canned text.

SG-9 (which gate scenario 1 overrides). §13.1 says only 'an override exercised once and visible in the report'; §3.6:1443 says the override disables THE NAMED GATE for exactly one next action in the same session. RESOLUTION: the override names the EDIT-SCOPE gate and is spent on one orchestrator edit inside the published item's fileScope (the deliberate alternative to an inline claim, and the one hatch whose effect is directly observable as a file on disk). The row asserts all four consequences: the first edit is allowed, the SECOND identical edit in the same session is re-denied, `taint[]` on the item and an `override` anomaly (core/types.ts:83) are written, and report.md names it. Picking a gate whose bypass produced no observable artifact would make the row untestable.

SG-10 (fixture verify command shape — the node-runner traps). The fixture's own suite is run by the REAL evidence engine with shell:false, so the §2.1 verify.scopes.unit.command must not fall into either trap scripts/test-conductor.sh:5-9 documents: a DIRECTORY positional (bogus red) or a ZERO-MATCH glob (vacuous green). RESOLUTION: the fixture's scope command is `["node","--test","tests/**/*.test.js"]` — one argv entry, expanded by node itself, matching at least one real file — with itemTest `["node","--test","{files}"]`; and row 13.1-fixture-suite-discriminates carries a CONTROL proving the fixture suite goes green with the subject present and red with it removed, so no later 'validate passed' row can be vacuous. This is the tools-9.4b.test.ts:370 controlSuite idiom applied to the e2e.

SG-11 (wall clock). Five scenarios over real child processes and real git can dominate the gate's runtime.
